name: Bauhaus
visualIdentity: Supplemental design reference, not a claimed source-collection label. Uses circles, squares, triangles, rules and lettering on a shared grid; asymmetry is balanced by deliberate proportion. Primary-color geometry alone does not establish Bauhaus.
suitableUses: Explicit fits include posters and identity built from primitives. Metadata also lists product and UI storytelling, editorial or minimalist layouts, motion posters, staged compositions and design education. These are suitability suggestions, not source-video facts.
limitations: Avoid hierarchy shifts that do not explain the subject, cropping important details, unsafe text areas or disruptive pinning. Omit chaptering when unnecessary, when transitions obscure causality, or when a continuous shot or loop would be broken. Grid size, BPM and beat count are optional parameters, not defining features.
palette: For new work without an approved palette, suggested roles are white background (#FFFFFF), black foreground (#000000), red accent (#D62828), yellow accent (#F2C230) and blue accent (#164B9B). These are authored suggestions, not canonical colors. Preserve task, brand, source and semantic role assignments; keep flat fields discrete, with no added gradient hues. Check actual composited contrast; supplied ratios cover only opaque two-color pairs.
motionAndInteraction: Stage geometric assembly with growth, rotation and interlocking; use disciplined spacing, staggered timing and deliberate holds. A configurable grid and shared beat-event table are optional. For interactive HTML, compatible patterns include pinned internal hero recomposition, reversible chapter handoffs and scroll-led narrative states; keep the outer pin stable and release without a jump. Video must use timed states, never live scroll input. Pattern candidates require scene-level fit; none is mandatory.
audio: No fixed soundtrack, tempo, genre, voice or sound layer is required. Choose music, narration, effects, ambience or silence for the topic and brief; honor supplied audio choices. Beat synchronization is optional. Assemble and synchronize authorized audio with picture, preserving intelligibility and avoiding clipping or competing vocals.
assetRequirements: Use topic-appropriate geometry, lettering and supplied exact copy, with readable text windows and safe placement. SVG is suitable for scalable shapes, strokes, masks and clipping; p5.js is optional for deterministic procedural visuals. Load fonts and assets before animation. Do not assume source footage, audio assets or verified physical production are supplied.
combinations: Can stand alone. Optional shape-morph transitions should remain between primitives, keep flat colors with snapped changes, align endpoints to the grid, and avoid organic forms or distorted lettering. A beat-table timing layer adds no visuals. Pinned hero, chapter-transition and storytelling patterns are optional only when their actions fit the actual scene.
productionApproach: Choose visual renderer and motion engine by style, action, assets and fidelity; document each responsibility and use one owner per animated property. SVG with GSAP is a suitable route; optional renderers and animation libraries are not a required bundle. Keep state deterministic and seekable. HyperFrames is primary for assembly, timing, synchronization, validation and export; use Remotion only if unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required capability, and record why. Inspect representative frames and the decoded sequence.
